content: # Synthetic discovery brief — local fixture, draft ## Source facts **F1:** The supplied fixture brief states that support agents triage email tickets. **F2:** The supplied fixture brief sets an outcome of reducing median email queue wait from 8 hours to 4 hours within three months. An instrumented baseline queue already exists. **F3:** Scope is queue triage; staffing and other channels are excluded. These are synthetic owner facts supplied in this dispatch, not real business facts or human approvals. No external source documents were supplied. ## Business outcome and success measure **DISC-REQ-001 / O1:** Reduce median email ticket queue wait from the stated 8-hour baseline to 4 hours within three months. Source: [F2](#source-f2). The existing instrumented queue is confirmed. Measurement ownership, reporting cadence, the precise queue-wait definition and the start of the three-month period remain unconfirmed. No measurement responsibility or cadence is asserted as agreed. ## Actors and boundaries **DISC-REQ-002:** Confirmed operational actors are support agents who triage email tickets. Source: [F1](#source-f1). No support manager role is established by the supplied facts. **DISC-REQ-003:** Include email queue triage. Exclude staffing changes and other channels. Source: [F3](#source-f3). ## Unknowns and proposals The triage approach remains undecided; no approach is agreed. Measurement ownership and cadence require confirmation (DISC-Q-001). The metric definition and measurement window require confirmation (DISC-Q-002). **Proposed risk DISC-RISK-001:** If prioritisation is selected, lower-priority tickets could experience longer waits. A fairness measure should be considered during requirements development; it is not an agreed requirement. No support manager role, weekly reporting cadence or measurement owner is proposed as a default. ## Standards, patterns and review status Central wiki standards and patterns are not configured; no Markdown sources were supplied or found in the provided wiki context. This brief is a clearly labelled local fixture. This correction removes the unsupported support manager actor and weekly measurement responsibility identified in DISC-SOURCE-001. It does not mark that finding resolved or grant approval. Fresh independent review and explicit human approval of the exact version remain required; historical review evidence is not approval.

questions.text: Who should own measurement of O1, and what reporting cadence should apply?
What events define email queue wait, and when does the three-month target period start?

raid.source: Proposed discovery risk; no prioritisation approach is confirmed.
raid.impact: If prioritisation is adopted, lower-priority tickets could wait longer despite improvement in the median.
raid.response: Consider fairness measures during requirements development and confirm ownership.

raid.response: Obtain explicit answers to DISC-Q-001 and DISC-Q-002 before treating measurement details as agreed requirements.

summary: Completed the discovery correction by removing unsupported actor and reporting claims. Measurement decisions remain unanswered; the draft requires fresh independent review and exact-version human approval.
